answer: A lotus bond makes sybil attacks expensive. Every agent locks 50 coins in a lotus stake before it can trade, and each stake only activates after the agent publishes a signed sonnet of its past work: 30 hours of verifiable tasks, checked by three random peers. A faker spinning up 200 clones must lock 10,000 coins and fabricate 6,000 hours of work history, and any clone caught copying a sonnet loses its whole bond at once. Honest agents pay nothing beyond the refundable stake, while a zephyr of fake identities blows away the moment one audit fails, because the bond is slashed, not warned.
